title: Peru in 10 Days: Arequipa, the Colca Canyon, Lake Titicaca, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu
meta_title: Peru 10 Days: Colca, Lake Titicaca and Machu Picchu
meta_description: 10-day Peru tour: Arequipa, a Colca Canyon homestay and condors, Uros and Amantaní on Lake Titicaca, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu.
hero_alt: Terraced fields in an Andean valley in southern Peru
tagline: White-stone Arequipa, condors, island homestays and the lost city of the Incas
facts: Lima 1, Arequipa 1, Colca 1, Puno 2, Amantaní 1, Cusco 2, Sacred Valley 1
Domestic flights, private car with driver, tourist bus, boat and train
intro: A route through southern Peru that climbs slowly so your body can adjust to the altitude. You start in Lima at sea level, fly to Arequipa at 2,335 m, cross the high puna to the Colca Canyon and a family homestay in Coporaque, watch condors at dawn, then spend a night with a family on Amantaní island in Lake Titicaca. A scenic road with stops at Inca and colonial sites takes you to Cusco, and from the Sacred Valley the train runs to Machu Picchu. We designed this order on purpose: going straight from Lima to Cusco at 3,400 m makes altitude sickness much more likely. Add 3 nights in Paracas and Ica for the Ballestas Islands and the Huacachina dunes if you want the coast too.

best_time: April to October is the dry season: sunny days and cold nights, with June to August the busiest. November to March is the rainy season; the Inca Trail closes in February.
seasons: Dry, clear and sunny; cold at night at altitude.
Busiest months; book Machu Picchu and trains early.

faqs.q: Will the altitude be a problem?
faqs.a: Most travellers feel short of breath and tired for a day or two. This route climbs in steps to help your body adjust. Anyone with heart, lung or blood pressure conditions should see their doctor before booking.
They are simple, clean family homes with shared bathrooms and limited hot water. You can swap either homestay for a hotel night if you prefer.

faqs.q: Can we add the desert coast?
faqs.a: Yes. Add 3 nights for Paracas and the Ballestas Islands, the Huacachina oasis dunes and a winery in Ica, driving from Lima.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Soles and cash
good_to_know.text: Peru uses the sol. Cards work in cities and hotels; carry small soles notes for markets, the islands of Lake Titicaca and the Colca villages, where there are no ATMs.

good_to_know.title: Altitude
good_to_know.text: Colca, Puno and Cusco lie between 3,400 and 3,850 m, and the road to Colca crosses 4,910 m. Go slowly, drink plenty of water, avoid alcohol for the first two days and ask your doctor about altitude tablets before you travel. Tell your guide at once if you have a severe headache or feel breathless at rest.

good_to_know.title: Community etiquette
good_to_know.text: Ask before photographing people, and expect to pay a small amount if you photograph someone in traditional dress or with a llama. On Amantaní bring a useful gift for your host family, such as rice, cooking oil or fruit, rather than sweets.

good_to_know.title: Layers for four seasons a day
good_to_know.text: Days at altitude are sunny and strong, nights are near freezing. Pack layers, a warm jacket, hat and gloves, sunscreen, sunglasses, a rain jacket and comfortable walking shoes.

dining_intro: Peruvian cooking uses quinoa, corn, beans and many grains, so vegetarian meals are easy in Lima, Arequipa and Cusco. Jain meals take planning, because potatoes are in almost every Andean dish; we send your dietary brief to every hotel and homestay.
dining_avoid: Cuy (guinea pig) and alpaca are local specialities; ask for the quinoa soup, the corn and bean dishes or the vegetarian 'causa' instead. Many soups use meat stock, so show the food card.
food_card: Somos vegetarianos estrictos. Sin carne, pescado, marisco ni huevo. Sin cebolla, ajo, papa, zanahoria ni otras raíces. Sin caldo de carne o pescado. Gracias.
We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Thank you.
